title: Feasibility of Kiesler Circle Training as a Standalone Intervention in an Outpatient Setting: A Transdiagnostic Pilot Study
summary:
The planned study involves three measurement points and investigates the Kiesler Circle group therapy approach (Guhn et al., 2025) in an outpatient setting. 
To reduce waiting times while still offering a treatment option relevant to the specific disorder, it can be beneficial for patients to first participate in a specialized group psychotherapy program before potentially receiving subsequent individual psychotherapy. The primary objective of the study is to examine the feasibility of Kiesler Circle group therapy as a standalone intervention within a mixed sample. Secondary objectives include gathering preliminary evidence regarding its efficacy in terms of symptom burden, interpersonal problems, and the ability to take the perspective of others.
The study will be conducted at the Research and Treatment Center for Mental Health in Bochum.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with depression, social phobia, and personality disorders are to be included, as interpersonal difficulties are typical for these patients (Guhn et al., 2025). Additionally, patients must have a score of over 1.6 on the Inventory of Interpersonal Problems (IIP-32; Thomas et al., 2011).
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are acute suicidality, substance dependence, and the presence of a psychotic or bipolar disorder.
